slides.text: Abacus AI DeepAgent Abacus AI DeepAgent - AI browser automation & scheduling tool Can schedule and execute recurring browser tasks autonomously: general AI reasoning real browser control task scheduling Opening websites, clicking through pages, gathering data, and sending results automatically at specified times (repeat daily, weekly, or monthly,...). Here are some examples: Opens LinkedIn, searches based on criteria, gathers contacts, drafts personalized outreach emails, and repeats the process every morning Job applications: Uploads resumes, processes job listings from Google Sheets, fills out forms, answers screening questions, and updates spreadsheets with submission status Invoice management: Logs into billing portals, downloads invoices, extracts data into spreadsheets, and emails summaries at scheduled times Website testing: Checks login systems, verifies order history updates, confirms download functionality, and reports results with screenshots Platform uses Abacus AI's Chat LLM, can use Claude, Gemini, ChatGPT, and Grok within one interface; combines reasoning modules with browser control APIs in a virtualized Chromium environment that maintains session state across runs. The system supports multilingual prompts and browser interactions, handling regional workflows across different languages Deep Agent completes standard browser tasks up to 2x as fast as competitors due to optimized latency between reasoning and execution steps Deep Agent Listener - desktop companion that records and transcribes meetings in real-time, answers questions about on-screen content, and integrates with Slack, CRM, and project management tools Coding agent can generate full-stack applications with payment integrations while the listener simultaneously documents the development process Pricing: $10 per month, providing full access to browser use, scheduling, and Chat LLM integration https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BWnfGzWXAps https://deepagent.abacus.ai https://abacus.ai/help/howTo/chatllm/deepagent_how_to https://abacus.ai/help/howTo/chatllm/deepagent_desktop_how_to https://abacus.ai

slides.title: AI Updates - 1 OpenAI AWS $38 Bln
slides.text: AI Updates - 1 OpenAI AWS $38 Bln deal OpenAI has signed a 7-year, $38 Bln deal with Amazon Web Services for cloud computing and AI infrastructure, including Nvidia GPUs OpenAI gets immediate access to crucial compute power This deal is marking a strategic shift of OpenAI to a multi-cloud approach beyond its existing Microsoft partnership AWS Trainium vs Nvidia Nvidia Blackwell GB200 outperforms Trainium2 by 3.85x in FP16 FLOPs Trainium2 excels in memory bandwidth per total cost of ownership (TCO), making it particularly competitive for memory-bound workloads like reinforcement learning and post-training techniques Amazon's strategy isn't to replace Nvidia but to provide choice and cost alternatives for AWS customers Major customers like Anthropic have committed to Trainium, reporting significant cost savings while helping design future chips through tight hardware-software co-design Nvidia's CUDA platform remains Trainium's biggest obstacle. Switching requires hundreds of hours of code rewriting and testing. AWS counters with its Neuron SDK, but it's still immature compared to CUDA's decade-long ecosystem of tools and developer support. Trainium3 is planned for late 2025, promises 4x performance over Trainium2 with 40% better energy efficiency, though it will consume over 1,000 watts per chip requiring liquid cooling. While Nvidia will likely maintain dominance for most AI workloads short-term, Trainium could capture significant market share in cost-sensitive enterprise training within AWS ecosystems

slides.title: Thinking about Thinking Anthropic paper titled "Emergent Introspective
slides.text: Thinking about Thinking Anthropic paper titled "Emergent Introspective Awareness in Large Language Models - https://www.anthropic.com/research/introspection Can AI models actually identify their own internal thoughts and distinguish them from externally injected concepts? Injected Thought Detection, Distinguishing Real vs. Injected Thoughts, Prefilled Response Awareness, Thought Control (Models were instructed to think or not think about specific words) Claude Opus 4.1 achieved roughly 20% success rates at detecting injected concepts when applied at appropriate layers and strengths, while other models performed at lower rates. Post-training was crucial for eliciting introspective awareness The research raises fundamental questions about AI consciousness by invoking Descartes' "I think, therefore I am". If models can genuinely identify their own thoughts versus injected ones, it challenges the prevailing view that LLMs are merely sophisticated next-token predictors https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qF9uOCxcvro Meta-Thinking. Thinking about thinking. Can AI do Philosophy? TL;DR: Useful Tool, Not Philosopher LLMs have developed significant meta-cognitive capabilities—the ability to reflect on and regulate their own thinking processes—though whether they can genuinely "do philosophy" remains deeply contested Recent research reveals that frontier AI models demonstrate multiple forms of meta-thinking. Modern LLMs exhibit self-evaluation abilities, error correction, and even latent-space planning behaviors. For instance, Claude-3.5-Haiku shows advanced goal-directed planning when composing poetry, first anticipating suitable rhyme words and then generating preceding content accordingly—demonstrating structured, multi-faceted meta-cognition rather than simple token-by-token generation Chain-of-thought prompting exemplifies AI meta-cognition by having models articulate intermediate reasoning steps before producing answers, significantly enhancing performance on complex tasks. Models fine-tuned on high-risk domains can independently identify and label their outputs as "dangerous" without explicit instructions, indicating internalized risk-awareness characteristic of meta-cognitive systems But current systems struggle with autonomous philosophical innovation—they excel at recapitulating classic arguments and identifying established lines of reasoning but fail to produce truly novel philosophical insights Genuine philosophical thinking operates to solve problems pertinent to oneself, requiring the kind of embodied, phenomenological experience that non-sentient systems cannot possess. AI cannot draw on personal experiences, physical sensations, or the awareness of mortality that often drives philosophical inquiry.

slides.title: Diffusion Models Diffusion Models as powerful alternatives to
slides.text: Diffusion Models Diffusion Models as powerful alternatives to LLLMs DMs generate outputs through iterative refinement of entire sequences simultaneously, unlike LLMs which produce tokens sequentially from left to right DMs outperform autoregressive models when trained on the same amount of data, and critically, they can reuse training data up to 100 times compared to only 4 times for LLMs before diminishing returns occur Since data scarcity has become a more significant bottleneck than compute power for scaling AI systems, this efficiency of using data makes diffusion models increasingly attractive Diffusion models map inputs into an n-dimensional vector space using variational autoencoders, where real data occupies high-value regions resembling "mountains" During training, noise is progressively added to original inputs, creating paths from high-value (original) to low-value (noisy) regions. Generation works by taking an input query, converting it to a vector, then using gradient descent to navigate toward the nearest "tallest mountain" representing optimal output. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Yu4ZWy1GjlE https://www.ibm.com/think/news/diffusion-models-llms https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.09992 https://cs231n.stanford.edu/slides/2023/lecture_15.pdf Gaurav Sen

slides.title: Keyword+Semantic search instead of RAG Keyword+Semantic search instead
slides.text: Keyword+Semantic search instead of RAG Keyword+Semantic search instead of RAG BM25 keyword search + Semantic search wirth embeddings Hybrid search stops at retrieval, while RAG adds a generation step using an LLM Without LLM we get simpler much pipelines compared to RAG Using Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF) to combine results together Tiger Data's - Agentic Postgres - a specialized PostgreSQL variant designed for AI agent workflows https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kegJPEoYBjw https://github.com/amrrs/hybrid-search/tree/main You don't need two separate tables - the best practice is to use a single table with both a BM25 index and a vector index on different columns, then combine results using  RRF Use PostgreSQL with extensions: ParadeDB for BM25 + pgvector for vectors (most popular) pg_textsearch for BM25 + pgvector​ CREATE TABLE documents ( id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY, title TEXT, content TEXT, embedding VECTOR(1536)  -- or your embedding dimension ); CREATE INDEX ON documents USING bm25(content); CREATE INDEX ON documents USING hnsw (embedding vector_cosine_ops); Run two separate queries against the same table, then merge results using Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF) WITH bm25_results AS ( SELECT id, pdb.score(id) AS score FROM documents WHERE content ||| 'your search query' ORDER BY score DESC LIMIT 20 ), vector_results AS ( SELECT id, 1 - (embedding <=> query_embedding) AS score FROM documents ORDER BY embedding <=> query_embedding LIMIT 20 ), rrf_scores AS ( SELECT id, SUM(1.0 / (60 + rank)) AS rrf_score FROM ( SELECT id, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY score DESC) AS rank FROM bm25_results UNION ALL SELECT id, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY score DESC) AS rank FROM vector_results ) combined GROUP BY id ) SELECT d.*, r.rrf_score FROM documents d JOIN rrf_scores r ON d.id = r.id ORDER BY r.rrf_score DESC LIMIT 10;

slides.title: Reflection.AI - $2 Bln at $8 Bln valuation
slides.text: Reflection.AI - $2 Bln at $8 Bln valuation Reflection AI is a startup founded in San Francisco, CA in March 2024 by two former Google DeepMind researchers— Misha Laskin (who led reward modeling for Gemini) and Ioannis Antonoglou (co-creator of AlphaGo) The company is building superintelligent autonomous coding systems using reinforcement learning and LLMs Reflection AI positions itself as an open-source alternative to closed frontier AI labs like OpenAI and Anthropic, and as a Western counterpart to Chinese AI firms like DeepSeek Rather than building general-purpose AI tools, the company focuses specifically on creating the best autonomous coding systems in the world The company launched Asimov (July 2025) , a breakthrough code comprehension agent designed to help engineers deeply understand complex codebases Unlike traditional AI coding tools like Copilot that provide autocompletion, Reflection AI's systems act as true software engineers capable of writing, debugging, and optimizing code autonomously Use reinforcement learning to train AI models that can simulate problem-solving, similar to how AlphaGo mastered the game of Go In October 2025, Reflection AI raised $2 Bln at $8 Bln valuation. This is a remarkable 15x increase from its $545 Mln valuation 7 months earlier The company has recruited top talent from DeepMind and OpenAI and built an advanced AI training stack that will be open for all With a team of about 60 AI researchers and engineers, Reflection AI has secured a compute cluster and plans to release a frontier language model in 2026 trained on "tens of trillions of tokens" https://reflection.ai https://docs.reflection.ai/docs/about-asimov https://www.sequoiacap.com/article/reflection-ai-asimov/ https://www.linkedin.com/company/reflectionai Misha Laskin and Ioannis Antonoglou

slides.title: OpenMemory VSCode Extension OpenMemory VS-Code Extension https://github.com/CaviraOSS/OpenMemory -
slides.text: OpenMemory VSCode Extension OpenMemory VS-Code Extension https://github.com/CaviraOSS/OpenMemory - MIT License https://openmemory.cavira.app https://openmemory.cavira.app/docs/introduction Modular AI memory engine provides persistent, structured, and semantic memory for LLM applications Enables AI agents, assistants, and copilots to remember user data, preferences, and prior interactions The extension automatically integrates with GitHub Copilot, Cursor, Claude Desktop, Windsurf, Codex, and any MCP-compatible AI Install the extension, start the OpenMemory server, and your AI tools instantly access your entire coding memory. Auto-configuration on first run Tracks every file edit, save, and open automatically Smart compression reduces token usage by 30-70% Query responses under 80ms with intelligent caching Real-time token savings and compression metrics Supports both Direct HTTP and MCP protocol modes 2–3× faster contextual recall, 6–10× lower cost, and full transparency compared to hosted “memory APIs” like Zep or Supermemory. Its multi-sector cognitive model allows explainable recall paths, hybrid embeddings (OpenAI / Gemini / Ollama / local), and real-time decay OpenMemory was created by: CaviraOSS (Cavira Open Source Software) git clone https://github.com/caviraoss/openmemory.git cd openmemory/backend cp .env.example .env npm install npm run dev # The server runs on http://localhost:8080 Note on Naming Confusion: There's a separate OpenMemory Chrome Extension and OpenMemory MCP created by the Mem0 team , which is a different project despite sharing a similar name. The Mem0 version focuses on browser-based memory syncing across AI tools like ChatGPT, Claude, and Perplexity, while the CaviraOSS OpenMemory is a more comprehensive self-hosted memory engine with hierarchical memory decomposition architecture

slides.title: Google AI for Science Supervised Reinforcement Learning (SRL)
slides.text: Google AI for Science Supervised Reinforcement Learning (SRL) - a novel training framework that teaches small 7B parameter models to reason through complex problems by combining two traditionally opposite approaches. The method breaks expert solutions into step-wise trajectories , where models generate hidden reasoning in "think tags" before producing each action, then receive immediate dense rewards based on string similarity comparisons . Testing on the Qwen 2.5 7B model has shown dramatic improvements Google's Gemini-powered multi-agent system functions as a collaborative research tool that generates hypotheses, designs experiments, and analyzes complex datasets The system uses specialized agents: - generation agents brainstorm ideas through internal debate - reflection agents act as peer reviewers , - ranking agents use ELO tournaments to select top hypotheses , - evolution agents merge promising concepts, - meta-review agents continuously improve the system Example: In partnership with Stanford University, the AI co-scientist identified vorinostat—an FDA-approved cancer drug —as a potential treatment for liver fibrosis Example: working with Imperial College London on a decade-long bacterial mystery about CFPICs (capsid-forming phage inducible chromosomal islands) , the AI independently reconstructed the "tail piracy" mechanism—where genetic hitchhikers build DNA-filled heads but steal tails from other phages—using only pre-discovery data. What took human researchers 10 years to solve, the AI figured out in days Human oversight remains essential for evaluating AI output, but the acceleration in discovery speed represents a fundamental shift in how scientific research can be conducted https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ANICPVqJ2ps https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.25992 https://research.google/blog/accelerating-scientific-breakthroughs-with-an-ai-co-scientist/

slides.title: Google Project Suncatcher Google Project Suncatcher - AI
slides.text: Google Project Suncatcher Google Project Suncatcher - AI data centers in space Using solar-powered satellite constellations (81 satellites) on sun-synchronous low-Earth orbit (400 miles above earth surface) Space-based solar panels can generate 8x more energy than on the surface (because there is no atmospheric interference). Equipped with TPUs (Tensor Processing Units) and connected by optical lasers Trillium-generation TPUs survived particle accelerator tests simulating space radiation at nearly three times the expected 5-year mission dose; Off-the-shelf components achieved required bandwidth for distributed machine learning tasks; The critical barrier is launch cost. Launch prices must drop below $200 per kilogram. Current costs range from $1,500 to $20,000 per kilogram. However, based on SpaceX's 20% learning rate (price drops 20% for every doubling of cumulative mass launched), Google projects launch costs could reach $200 per kilogram by around 2035 if SpaceX maintains approximately 180 Starship launches annually Google plans to launch two prototype satellites in partnership with Planet Labs by early 2027 https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XlSQZKY_gCg

slides.title: Why Sam Altman was fired in 2023 In
slides.text: Why Sam Altman was fired in 2023 In November 2023 Sam Altman was fired from OpenAI Ilya Sutskever's deposition in the Elon Musk v. Sam Altman lawsuit reveals that he and Mira Murati plotted for over a year to remove Sam Altman from OpenAI Ilya has created a 52-page memo and separate document about Greg Brockman to present to independent board directors (Helen Toner, Adam D'Angelo, and Tasha McCaulay) because he feared Sam would "make the discussions disappear" if he learned about them This memo accused Sam of exhibiting "a consistent pattern of lying, undermining his execs, and pitting his execs against one another," with Ilya recommending termination as the appropriate action Most screenshots and information came from Mira Murati, and Ilya used disappearing emails to prevent leaks The deposition revealed several conflicts within OpenAI's leadership. Dario Amodei (before founding Anthropic) wanted Greg Brockman fired and himself placed in charge of all research, but Sam didn't accept or reject these conditions, which Ilya viewed as problematic Ilya found board member Helen Toner's October 2023 article praising Anthropic and criticizing OpenAI "not far from obviously inappropriate" and discussed potentially removing her from the board with Sam Within 24-48 hours of Sam's removal, Anthropic proposed merging with OpenAI and taking over its leadership. Ilya opposed the merger. Ilya characterized the removal process as "rushed" due to the board's inexperience in board matters https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mGBh2EAk7j0

slides.title: Elon Musk $1T Compensation Package Elon Musk's unprecedented
slides.text: Elon Musk $1T Compensation Package Elon Musk's unprecedented compensation package was approved by Tesla shareholders on November 6, 2025 This new pay plan could potentially be worth up to $1 Trillion over the next decade Musk doesn't receive a traditional salary, so the entire package comes in the form of stock options. If he receives all shares from this package over ten years, it would equate to approximately $275 million per day The payouts are contingent on Tesla achieving specific market capitalization targets. The first tranche will be awarded when Tesla reaches a $2 trillion market cap, compared to its current valuation of $1.54 trillion. Subsequent tranches require the company's valuation to increase by $500 billion increments up to $6.5 trillion, with the final two tranches requiring $1 trillion increments each. For Musk to receive the complete package, Tesla must achieve an $8.5 trillion market cap—a 466% increase from current levels The approval increases Musk's voting stake in Tesla from approximately 13% to 25%, addressing his previous concerns about leading the company without at least 20% voting power This new package comes while Musk's previous 2018 compensation plan worth $55.8 billion remains tied up in Delaware courts, where a judge ruled that shareholders lacked sufficient information to assess the board-approved compensation. The Delaware Supreme Court is currently reviewing Tesla's appeal

slides.title: FDE - Hottest new job in AI A
slides.text: FDE - Hottest new job in AI A Forward-Deployed Engineer (FDE) is a software engineer who embeds directly with customer teams on-site (or work closely) to build and deploy custom AI solutions tailored to their specific business problems. AI implementation has become the new bottleneck - the challenge is no longer building models, but deploying them effectively in complex, real-world environments. OpenAI established its FDE team at the start of 2025 and expects to grow it to about 50 engineers this year. Anthropic, and Cohere are rapidly hiring these hybrid professionals too. The term “forward-deployed” originates from the military (like "airborne troops") and was popularized by Palantir , which sends embedded engineers into client environments to co-create solutions. The role has been dubbed " the hottest job in tech " by venture capital firm a16z (Andreessen Horowitz) FDEs command top salaries due to their high-impact nature . Many FDEs become trusted advisors within organizations and later transition to founding startups or leadership roles, thanks to their unique blend of technical and business experience FDE is the Hottest new job in AI. Job listings for FDEs have surged over 800% in 2025 . A year ago the hottest AI job was prompt engineer
